key_insight: MxGPS shows that joint training on complementary power-grid tasks can prevent topology overfitting and improve zero-shot generalization across unseen grids.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a compact, parameter-efficient path toward foundation models that remain reliable when deployed on new power network topologies.
method: Multiplex graph transformer with K task-specialized GPS branches over a shared node encoder
Self-supervised pre-training plus multi-task fine-tuning on SSE and AC power flow
Cross-branch attention module evaluated in ablation
evidence_signal: Across a 3-fold sliding-window evaluation on four unseen topologies (14-, 24-, 162-, and 300-bus), MxGPS achieved 0% boundary violation rate on all zero-shot power flow cases and degrades only 39% under topology shift.
watch_item: Results are tied to specific SSE+PF training and topology-shift settings, so performance may vary if the target grid distribution, sensor quality, or task mix changes.
paper_title: MxGPS: Multiplex Graph Transformers for a Power Grid Foundation Model
